external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who borrows, renews and reserves books through the library app and uses self-service kiosks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: Members also scan their library cards and books at kiosks.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who use the circulation page to change loan and account records.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login; individual staff and branches cannot be distinguished in the history.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: The app on members' phones through which members borrow, renew and reserve books and which calls the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library cards and books and which sends loans and returns to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that is the service interface for loans, checks loan rules, changes loan and reservation records, and serves the circulation page.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Authentication is not established. Priya said: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." The sources disagree about exposure: Lending service note says "The lending API is internal-only"; Interview transcript says "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet."

processes.name: circulation page
processes.description: The circulation page served by the lending API for desk staff to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
processes.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
processes.notes: The page is served by the lending API.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The old reservations database was merged into this database and is gone.

data_flows.name: borrow books
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to request borrowing through the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Member and book information for a borrowing request

data_flows.name: renew loan
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to request a loan renewal through the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: what happens when someone renews a loan or reserves a title in the app.
data_flows.data_description: Member and book information for a loan renewal

data_flows.name: reserve title
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to request a title reservation through the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the app asks for a title and the API puts the member in the queue for it.
data_flows.data_description: Member and title information for a reservation

data_flows.name: send loans
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends each loan to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.data_description: Member card, book and loan information

data_flows.name: send returns
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: Member card, book and return information

data_flows.name: change loan record
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page to extend a loan, clear an account block or mark a book returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
data_flows.notes: The shared desk login uses a password taped under the desk.
data_flows.data_description: Member account, loan and return information

data_flows.name: read and write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations, addresses and borrowing histories

trust_boundaries.name: phones
trust_boundaries.description: Members' phones on which the library app runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network where branch kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.
trust_boundaries.notes: Desk staff also work on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data centre where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it contains names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history; disclosure of this personal data would harm people.

assumptions.assumption: The circulation page is a separate web-facing process presented by the lending API.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it a circulation page and says the lending API serves it; it is modelled separately to represent the named interface used by desk staff.
